clue.text: Worried on day one, lacking nothing but a remedy

indicators.note: something worried is fretted and disturbed, so these words are shaken up into a new order
lacking means going without, so one item must be taken out of the fodder

parts.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone fretting on the first day, with nothing to help them except some medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop one O from ON DAY ONE and rearrange the remaining seven letters to get ANODYNE.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, an anodyne is a painkilling medicine, something that soothes and relieves suffering.

clue.text: Note father had a writing block

parts.note: taken as written
pa is an informal word for father
had is shortened to 'd, as in I'd

explanation.surface: A dad who could not think what to write in his message.
explanation.walkthrough: Writer's block is the surface reading; here the block is a physical pad of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A notepad is a stack of paper sheets glued at one edge, used for jotting things down.

clue.text: A new confidence, initially, in the heart of French ballet

indicators.note: being in the heart of something means sitting inside it, surrounded on both sides

parts.note: de is the French word for 'of', so 'of French' points to it

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each word in the phrase before it

parts.note: first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A new dancer gaining self-belief at the centre of a French ballet company.
explanation.walkthrough: The three initials sit inside DE, the French for 'of': D-ANC-E.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballet is one particular form of theatrical dance, so the general word covers it.

clue.text: Denies English agent's corruption

indicators.note: corruption spoils and distorts something, so these letters are scrambled out of shape

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English
taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A British spy flatly denies being corrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate a claim is to deny it or declare it untrue, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Gruesome, bare suspect follows Scot

indicators.note: follows means comes after, so the second element is placed behind the first

parts.note: Mac is a common nickname for a Scotsman

indicators.note: something suspect is dodgy and not straight, so the word before it is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grisly scene in which a naked suspect trails a Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Macabre describes something ghastly and dwelling on death, so it is a close synonym of gruesome.

clue.text: Partners behind a false report on extraterrestrials

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so this element is placed at the end

parts.note: taken as written
a lie is a false statement
North and South are partners in the card game bridge

explanation.surface: A couple concocting a bogus story about sightings of little green men.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North and South play as a pair, so partners can be N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliens in science fiction are beings from other planets, creatures not of this Earth.

clue.text: Be a square about a ballet posture

indicators.note: about suggests turning things around and moving them, so the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to be old-fashioned and dull when it comes to dance positions.
explanation.definitionFit: An arabesque is a classical dance pose standing on one leg with the other stretched out behind.

clue.text: Canister turned up with top removed for wine

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from the bottom upwards
in a down clue the top is the first letter, and that is removed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tin can that has been upended and opened to make room for wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the C of CANISTER, leaving ANISTER, then write it backwards: RETSINA.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Thieves cook help to serve to lunatics

indicators.note: serving something to someone sets it beside them, so the two parts are joined
to cook something is to doctor or falsify it, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: the setter must have meant kelp, a seaweed, since an H appears nowhere in the answer; read it as KELP TO
maniacs are wild, crazed people

explanation.surface: Thieves preparing food to dish up to the insane.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed the anagram fails: 'help to' has an H where KLEPTO needs a K. The setter surely wrote 'kelp', seaweed you could cook, which fits the surface better too.
explanation.definitionFit: Kleptomaniacs have a compulsion to steal, so they are habitual thieves, often of things they do not need.

clue.text: Surprise in the latest unbiased report

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the words of the phrase that follows

parts.note: the end of one word joined to the start of the next

explanation.surface: A shock revealed in a fair and impartial news bulletin.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the gap: lateST UNbiased.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to astonish or shock them, which is to surprise them greatly.

clue.text: Ivy, almost taken in by dashing men, gads about

indicators.note: being taken in by something means being swallowed up inside it

parts.note: gallants are stylish, chivalrous young men

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl called Ivy, swept off her feet by smart young men, goes out on the town.
explanation.walkthrough: Gallants is an old word for fashionable, chivalrous young men; split it after its fourth letter to take in the shortened name.
explanation.definitionFit: To gallivant is to roam around in search of pleasure, which is just what gadding about means.

clue.text: Optimistic over the rhythm

parts.note: over as in finished: time is up
the beat is the pulse or rhythm of music

explanation.surface: Feeling hopeful once the music ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Over and UP share the sense of finished, as in 'the game is up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Upbeat describes a cheerful, positive mood, the outlook of someone hopeful about the future.

clue.text: Denim cap causing widespread disease

indicators.note: causing suggests the words are made into something else, so their letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A jeans-fabric hat blamed for spreading an epidemic.
explanation.definitionFit: A pandemic is an outbreak of illness that spreads across countries or the whole world.

clue.text: Acceptance of notice by girl no one backed

indicators.note: by means next to, so the parts are placed side by side

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a public notice
miss is a title for a young unmarried woman

indicators.note: backed means put into reverse, so those words are read from right to left

parts.note: NO followed by I for one

explanation.surface: A girl ignored by everyone finally gets her acceptance through a public announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'no one' is turned around; the notice and the girl stay as they are. One is I, as so often in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Admission is being let in or accepted, as to a club, school or hospital.

clue.text: Briefly, I am to arbitrate at once

indicators.note: briefly means in shortened form, so a letter drops out of the contraction

parts.note: taken as written, then contracted
to mediate is to act as go-between in a dispute

explanation.surface: Someone declaring in short that they will settle the dispute straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: I AM shortened is I'M, as in everyday speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediate action happens instantly without any delay, so it is done right now.

clue.text: Peer in tie

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person of the same rank or standing as another
second meaning: to match a score or record

explanation.walkthrough: Peer looks like a verb for looking or a noun for a lord; tie looks like neckwear. Both are senses of being level.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means someone on a level with another; as a verb it means to draw level.

clue.text: Was confused by politician in Slough

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two parts sit together
confused means mixed up, so the word before it is jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A member of parliament baffled by a visit to Slough, the commuter town west of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough with a capital looks like the Berkshire town; here it is the common noun for boggy ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a stretch of soft, muddy ground or marsh, much like a bog or swamp.

clue.text: Tungsten found in two animals

parts.note: the first animal: a wild canine
the second animal: a male sheep

explanation.surface: A heavy metal turning up in a pair of creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two animals' supplies two separate words placed side by side, a wild canine followed by a male sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfram is the older, alternative name for the metallic element tungsten, symbol W.

clue.text: Support for the judiciary of someone not in the government?

definitions.text: of someone not in the government

parts.note: to back is to support
the bench is the collective term for judges

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone outside the government would support the judges.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK Parliament, MPs without government or shadow posts sit on the back benches.
explanation.definitionFit: A backbench MP is an ordinary member without a ministerial job, so the adjective describes such a person.

clue.text: Joints that are superior for a party

parts.note: knees are leg joints
up as in higher, above

explanation.surface: Top-quality cannabis cigarettes brought along to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: A knees-up is British slang for a lively party with dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A knees-up is an informal British word for a lively celebration or get-together.

clue.text: Accountant's dense, they say with a lowering of the voice

parts.note: CA stands for chartered accountant

indicators.note: they say means as it is spoken, so we want a word of matching sound but different spelling

parts.note: sounds like thick

explanation.surface: An accountant described as thick, who speaks more and more quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadence is the falling inflection of the voice, as at the end of a sentence.

clue.text: Miner has no right to dog

indicators.note: has no means lacks, so the following letter is taken away

parts.note: a collier is a coal miner
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A coal miner with no right to keep a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: COLLIER without its R.
explanation.definitionFit: A collie is a breed of sheepdog originally from Scotland.

clue.text: Pleased with one blending oil for flowers

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the parts are placed next to each other

parts.note: glad means pleased

indicators.note: blending mixes things together, so the word after it is stirred into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone happily mixing oils to make a floral perfume.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladioli are tall garden plants with sword-shaped leaves and spikes of showy blooms.

clue.text: Typify a figure that has me turning round at first

indicators.note: at first means placed at the front, ahead of the other piece
turning round means facing the other way, so that word is written backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a body is a physique or figure

explanation.surface: A model whose figure has me spinning round to look.
explanation.definitionFit: To embody a quality is to represent it perfectly, to be a typical example of it.

clue.text: Notable rising after the Spanish lost a weapon

indicators.note: lost means gone missing, so those letters are taken away
in a down entry, rising means read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A dignitary on the rise once the Spanish have dropped their arms.
explanation.walkthrough: NOTABLE reversed is ELBATON; take away EL to leave BATON.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a police officer's truncheon, a short club used as a weapon.

clue.text: Fear imprisonment in thatch?

parts.note: dread is great fear
to imprison is to lock someone up

explanation.surface: Being afraid of getting trapped in a straw roof.
explanation.walkthrough: Thatch is a roof of straw but also slang for a thick head of hair; the question mark flags the playful sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreadlocks are a hairstyle of long matted ropes, and a shaggy head of hair is jokingly called a thatch.

clue.text: Care for a number getting final demand

indicators.note: getting means receiving or gaining, so something is added on

parts.note: ten is a number

indicators.note: final points to the last letter of the next word

parts.note: last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Being looked after, a figure receives a last reminder to pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Final demand' looks like an unpaid bill; here it only means the last letter of demand.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend someone is to look after them, as a nurse tends the sick.

clue.text: Hampers M1 speed order

indicators.note: order means arrange, so the letters before it are put into a new sequence

parts.note: the digit 1 stands in for the letter I
taken as written

explanation.surface: A speed restriction holding up traffic on the M1, Britain's main north-south motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To impede is to obstruct or slow down progress, the same as getting in the way.

clue.text: Spider's in the cricket team

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a creature that spins webs
second meaning: a bowler who makes the ball turn

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a slow bowler who makes the ball turn sharply off the pitch is a spin bowler; the surface suggests an insect in a team of crickets.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiders produce silk and weave webs, and a slow bowler gives the ball rotation, so both turn thread or ball.
